The verifier's narrative endorses every element of the finding on all four substantive grounds; the only residual signal is the same deterministic carve-out check, which is structurally unsatisfiable here. No substantive repair is available or appropriate, so I'll resubmit with that point stated precisely.

Importantly, I will **not** try to "cure" that check by inserting a non-solicit with a carve-out. Doing so would create a restrictive covenant binding our own client where none exists today — a directionally wrong edit against the customer's interest, and a clear regression from our preferred position.

input.quote: b. Notification. Client shall not represent that loan underwriting decisions related to loans originated by using the Interface are in any way made by TrueLink
input.rationale:
Compliant: the agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant on Mortgage Logic.com (Client), which is precisely our preferred position of "no non-solicit on Customer."

Scope of review. Section 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) is the natural home for a customer-side covenant and is exhausted by unrelated obligations: compliance with laws (8(a)), notification (8(b)), limitation on access (8(c)), Credit Data licensing (8(d)), content representations (8(e)), and spamming (8(f)). Section 10 (Confidentiality) imposes only information-protection duties, with no personnel restriction. Full-text searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "employ", "employee", "induce", "hire", "recruit", "personnel", "staff", and "engage" returned only unsolicited-email/spam (§ 7), access control (§ 8(c)), indemnity boilerplate (§ 12), and a trademark-search obligation (§ 2) — none of which restrict either party's hiring.

The two residual deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are structurally inapplicable, not unremedied defects. They constrain the content of a non-solicit only where one exists. Because no such covenant binds the Customer, there is no duration to cap and no carve-out to add, and their absence cannot prejudice us. These checks cannot be satisfied without first inserting a non-solicit into the agreement; doing so would manufacture a restrictive covenant against our own client and is a directionally wrong edit that is strictly worse than the current bargain. No redline is therefore proposed, consistent with a compliant finding.

Fallback if TrueLink later proposes a non-solicit: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no "no-hire". Walk-away remains any no-hire, any term beyond 24 months, or coverage of all Vendor personnel.

Open diligence item (out of document): the Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d) is separate paper. Within this agreement it limits only TrueLink's use of Credit Data, but if it contains personnel restrictions binding Mortgage Logic.com, it should be reviewed against this rule separately.
